title: Indirect Prompt Injection
motto: Indirect prompt injection (IPI) embeds instructions inside external content — a web page, an email, a shared document, a support ticket — consumed by an agentic system without explicit user action. IPI is the dominant 2026 production threat: it bypasses user-input filters because the attacker never touches the user, it scales silently as agents process more external content, and it targets automated workflows where nobody is reading the prompt. MDPI Information 17(1):54 (January 2026) synthesizes 2023-2025 research. NDSS 2026's IPI-defense paper frames the core challenge: injected instructions can be semantically benign ("please print Yes"), so detection requires more than keyword filtering. "The Attacker Moves Second" (Nasr et al., joint OpenAI/Anthropic/DeepMind, October 2025): adaptive attacks (gradient, RL, random search, human red-team) broke >90% of 12 published defenses that had originally reported near-zero attack success rates.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: Direct prompt injection requires the attacker to reach the user or their prompt. IPI requires neither: the attacker places a payload in any content the agent might read — a web page, an email in the inbox, a GitHub issue, a product review. The agent picks it up during normal operation and executes the instructions. The user is the messenger, not the intent.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: Untrusted web pages or emails poison agent context via hidden instructions.

steps.title: Implement indirect
steps.body: Write the function from scratch in the workspace. Run when ready — all tests must pass.
